feed.title: NPR Programs: All Things Considered
feed.subtitle: All Things Considered hosts Ailsa Chang, Mary Louise Kelly, Juana Summers and Scott Detrow present the program's trademark mix of news, interviews, commentaries, reviews, and offbeat features 7 days a week.

entry.title: Lindsay Clancy jury fails to reach a consensus on sixth day of deliberations
entry.summary: There was drama in the courtroom Thursday in the trial of the Massachusetts mother charged with murdering her three children. The jury has been trying to reach consensus for six days.

entry.title: International forecasters warn countries need to be prepared for a powerful El Niño
entry.summary: Forecasters are expecting the El Niño weather pattern to strengthen significantly this year, raising the risks of extreme weather around the world well into 2027.

entry.title: Why the U.S. Treasury is buying back double the government bonds it normally does
entry.summary: The U.S. Treasury is planning to buy back at least double the long-dated government bonds it usually does. Will the plan pit the Treasury secretary against both the bond markets and the Fed?

entry.title: Gloria Steinem helped shape the classic children's album 'Free to Be... You and Me'
entry.summary: Through Ms. Magazine, the late activist and author Gloria Steinem was one of the driving forces behind one of the most classic children's albums, Free to Be... You and Me from 1972.

entry.title: Immigration policies prompt differing messages from Republicans and Democrats
entry.summary: Republicans see immigration as a winning issue ahead of the midterms as President Trump's administration ramps up arrests and deportations.

entry.title: As El Niño intensifies, Rio turns to science — and a spiritual advisor
entry.summary: This year's Super El Niño has brought unprecedented weather to Rio de Janeiro. Unaccustomed to tornado-strength winds, the city found an unusual partner to combat the weather: a spiritual adviser.

entry.title: Nepali community in Texas grieves and prays for healing after flash floods
entry.summary: Nepalese groups in North Texas, which has one of the largest communities of people from Nepal in the U.S., continue to grieve the loss of hundreds of people after the devastating floods in August.

entry.title: Filmmaker Abigail Disney remembers her friendship with the late activist Gloria Steinem
entry.summary: NPR's Ailsa Chang speaks with filmmaker Abigail Disney about her friendship with Gloria Steinem and the legacy her friend leaves behind.

entry.title: Gloria Steinem in her own words
entry.summary: Gloria Steinem used her voice to fight for women's rights throughout her long life. We take time to revisit some of her conversations with NPR, and share some unreleased writings.

entry.title: Swing voters say Trump hasn't delivered on his promise to lower prices
entry.summary: As the midterms near, NPR's Tamara Keith has another installment of her Swing Shift project. Three swing voters in Pennsylvania tell us what affordability means to them.
